chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:
Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) said, "I am the Martyr of Tears. No believer remembers me without crying."

key_terms.أَنَا: I; referring to Imam Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قَتِيلُ الْعَبْرَةِ: Martyr of Tears; a title for Imam Husayn indicating that his memory causes believers to weep
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: Believer; a follower of Islam who remembers the Imams

ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Martyr of Tears' signify regarding Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this profound title, 'Qatil al-'Abrat' (The Martyr of Tears), linking Imam al-Husayn’s sacrifice directly to the spiritual sensitivity of the believers. This narration underscores the Shia theological concept that remembering the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely historical recollection but an emotional and spiritual act of devotion that manifests in tears, serving as a sign of true faith.
